t: This is the site of the Marshalsea, a notorious prison in Southwark, just south of the Thames. It stood from 1373 to 1842. It held men accused of crimes at sea and political figures charged with sedition, but it's best known for imprisoning London's poorest debtors. In the eighteenth century, over half of England's prisoners were jailed for debt. William Odell, an Irish Member of Parliament for Limerick, died here in 1831.
